video_title: Jensen Huang is Out at Nvidia & Bitcoin is Crashing?!
gist: Jordi Visser tells Anthony Pompliano that Jensen Huang's abrupt scandal-driven exit from Nvidia is a sentiment hit (price targets cut, EPS unchanged) that should fade because AI is inevitable, while Bitcoin's slide to ~$69K is a liquidity story tied to gold and the biggest weekly 2-year yield jump since 2022 amid a hawkish Fed. He pushes back on CZ's 'not enough money for AI mega-IPOs' theory and frames tokenization and agentic commerce as Bitcoin's real long-term driver.

themes.theme: Jensen Huang ouster and Nvidia fallout

insights.claim: Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia within roughly four to five days of a scandal breaking (alleged extramarital affairs, including with a subordinate and a rumored Chinese spy), after 33 years building the company; the CFO stepped in as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Leadership vacuum at the most important AI hardware company is a new idiosyncratic risk for NVDA holders through the search process.

insights.claim: After Huang's exit, Wall Street analysts cut Nvidia price targets dramatically but did not change earnings forecasts, implying the selloff is a multiple/sentiment hit rather than a fundamentals downgrade.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A gap between unchanged EPS estimates and lower targets is where a de-rating can reverse if upcoming earnings confirm demand.
insights.quote: Everyone lowered their price targets dramatically, but no one changed their earnings forecasts.

insights.claim: Visser expects the Huang scandal to fade relatively quickly for markets because Nvidia's demand backlog means earnings will keep growing over the next few years regardless of who is CEO, unless further undisclosed facts emerge about Nvidia's own conduct.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Treat the drawdown as a potential entry if next week's earnings hold up; the tail risk is new revelations about company conduct.
insights.quote: nobody's going to remember this in 6 months

insights.claim: Visser uses Steve Jobs as precedent: Jobs was diagnosed with cancer around the iPhone launch in 2007, took leave in 2009 and died in 2011, yet Apple thrived because the innovation wave mattered more than who ran the company.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: When a founder-CEO leaves during an exponential product cycle, the cycle can carry the stock; focus on demand, not personality.

insights.claim: Visser argues exponential innovation was the only thing that mattered for markets for roughly 13-15 years leading into ChatGPT, overriding rates, QE and European crises, and that AI will play the same role going forward.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Macro gyrations are secondary to positioning in the dominant innovation wave over multi-year horizons.
insights.quote: AI is inevitable. Like there's no way to stop it.

insights.claim: Visser thinks Nvidia should avoid M&A to acquire a new CEO (e.g., Lisa Su of AMD was floated) because integration adds risk on top of Huang's absence, citing Marvell's stock falling violently after announcing a merger.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: An acquisition-driven succession would be a negative signal; a quiet internal or hired successor is the bullish path.

insights.claim: Visser says it is too early to identify which competitors benefit from Nvidia's leadership turmoil, though Google gets mentioned for its own chips, and Elon Musk publicly said it would be his honor to hire Huang (speculatively for Terrafab).
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Watch for share shifts toward custom silicon only if Nvidia's execution actually slips.

insights.claim: Visser suspects there is more to the Huang story involving US-China geopolitics, noting reports that Scott Bessent and Lutnick are clashing and being blamed over what they knew, and expects more to come out over the next month.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Headline risk on NVDA and China chip policy may persist for weeks; geopolitics could reshape export policy.
insights.quote: It's just too important of a story and he's too important of a person for governments to not be involved.

insights.claim: Despite Nvidia stock falling sharply on the Huang news and a Fed official floating a 50 basis point move in December, the rest of the stock market held up that week.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Market resilience to concentrated bad news suggests the damage is idiosyncratic, not systemic.

insights.claim: Visser believes open-source and frontier AI models will coexist and share revenues, with Anthropic, OpenAI and Google dominating the frontier side, and that the Huang episode does not change that trajectory.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Don't trade the open- vs closed-source narrative off this scandal; both models monetize.

themes.theme: Bitcoin as a liquidity asset tracking gold and 2-year yields

insights.claim: Visser attributes Bitcoin's fall to around $69,000 to macro liquidity: the week saw the largest one-week rise in two-year yields (about 35 basis points) since 2022, and Bitcoin has traded with gold since March due to liquidity headwinds.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Track 2-year Treasury yields and gold as the near-term driver of BTC rather than crypto-native news.
insights.quote: We just had the largest rise in two-year yields in a week, 35 basis points uh since 2022. So that's why Bitcoin is down.

insights.claim: Visser frames Bitcoin as having two components: an innovation side that trades with the AI trade and a liquidity side that trades like gold with rate expectations.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Decompose BTC moves into AI-risk and rates/liquidity factors to anticipate correlation regimes.
insights.quote: I think of Bitcoin as being two separate parts. One is the innovation side and the other one is the liquidity side.

insights.claim: Visser expects liquidity headwinds to become tailwinds next year as inflation pressures fade, but says the Fed is not there yet and Bitcoin needs inflation headwinds to lessen before it benefits.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: BTC upside is gated on a dovish inflation turn; patience until CPI/PCE roll over.

insights.claim: Visser says a possible catalyst for the next rally is the Fed not delivering the 50 basis point December move that is already priced into the market.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: An undershoot vs. priced-in hawkishness in December could spark a risk-asset and Bitcoin rally.
insights.quote: don't be surprised if the catalyst for the next, you know, rally, isn't December where we don't do 50. We've already built 50 into the market.

insights.claim: Visser argues that tokenization and agentic commerce, not demographics, are what will drive fiat capital (he cites ~$900 trillion in the fiat system vs. a $3-4 trillion crypto market) on chain, with Bitcoin serving as the collateral backing of the digital system.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The long-term BTC bull case depends on on-chain asset and transaction volumes; track tokenization adoption by institutions.
insights.quote: Once you start moving things on chain, Bitcoin is the collateral backing of the digital system.

insights.claim: Visser says the Bitcoin community is already long, so price gains require new buyers from pension funds, insurers, hedge funds and mutual funds who are convinced by tokenization fundamentals; MicroStrategy's index removals have a trading impact but are not the core issue.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Index-flow selling from MSTR removal is a short-term overhang; institutional tokenization interest is the real driver to watch.

themes.theme: Hawkish Fed despite cooling inflation inputs

insights.claim: Visser notes inflation fears are broad-based, with many components of PCE and CPI above 3%, which is why Fed officials are hawkish even beyond the Iran war's impact on headline inflation.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Broad-based core inflation keeps hike risk alive even if oil eases.

insights.claim: Visser highlights that Brent crude is back to its early-March level when the Iran war started (on contracts about six months out), and livestock and agricultural futures are at 52-week lows after falling off in September.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Commodity inputs to inflation have already rolled over, supporting a later dovish pivot.

insights.claim: DRAM prices, a major contributor to this year's inflation (Apple said it had to raise prices), have seen year-over-year growth decelerate from about 900% to about 250%, so the second derivative has turned down.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Decelerating memory prices ease goods inflation but also signal peak pricing power for memory makers.
insights.quote: we were up 900%, now we're up 250% year-over-year. So you're already getting the second derivative turning down

insights.claim: Visser says inflation swaps are at the lows of the year and inflation expectations are anchored, yet nearly every Fed official this week called for higher rates, which he finds surprising and expects means at least two more hikes.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Market-implied inflation contradicts Fed rhetoric; a gap that tends to close via Fed softening once data cooperates.
insights.quote: they seem to be driven towards knocking inflation down. And that means there's probably at least two more hikes.

insights.claim: Visser points out that Kevin Warsh said he wanted the Fed to be forward-looking with less forward guidance and less Fed speaking, yet the week featured a wave of Fed officials jawboning for hikes, and he expects jawboning to continue for months if oil stays elevated.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Fed communication is inconsistent with its leadership's stated framework; expect volatility around Fed speakers.

themes.theme: AI trade positioning, capital supply and IPO wave

insights.claim: Visser says the AI trade was hurt because by May-June everyone was long, and then a wave of capital raising hit the market (the ~$80 billion Google deal, SpaceX in June) just as buying power was exhausted, followed by a hedge fund deleveraging in late October/early November.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Supply of new AI equity against crowded positioning, not demand weakness, drove the drawdown; watch issuance calendars.
insights.quote: just when everyone was long the AI trade, we started pounding the market with capital raising.

insights.claim: Visser disagrees with CZ's claim that mega-IPOs (SpaceX at $1.5-2T, Anthropic at $1.2-1.5T, OpenAI at $1.5-2T) exceed available money and will force money printing; he says there is ample capital (~$250-300T in global stocks and bonds plus ~$600T illiquid), though liquid capital is constrained and buyers must sell something else.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Mega-IPOs will be funded by selling legacy holdings, pressuring old-economy index constituents rather than requiring QE.
insights.quote: I do agree that there's a limit to who can buy these things right now on the liquid side

insights.claim: Visser notes Anthropic is only raising about $80 billion in its IPO rather than its full valuation, and that over $1 trillion has been raised this year, including $122 billion by OpenAI earlier in the year.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Size of actual float, not headline valuation, determines how much liquidity the IPO absorbs.

insights.claim: Visser expects investors to sell holdings like Ford and GM in the S&P 500 to fund purchases of SpaceX and other AI mega-IPOs, a rotation that weeds out companies that will not survive.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Legacy index constituents face funding-source selling around AI mega-IPOs.
insights.quote: people would rather own SpaceX than that

insights.claim: Visser says he put a good amount of money into semiconductor names the prior week, doing well on two of them while Nvidia was hit by the Huang situation, and expects AI names to trade more on fundamentals and higher next year now that the over-owned situation has cleared.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The speaker is positioned long semis after the flush, betting positioning has reset.

insights.claim: Visser identifies three major catalysts before year-end: the Anthropic IPO (likely next week), Nvidia earnings (no major surprises expected), and the December Fed meeting.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Calendar the Anthropic IPO trading, NVDA earnings, and the Fed as the key risk events into year-end.

insights.claim: As a trader, Visser watches whether the market keeps closing above its open and making its intraday lows in the morning; the market had a good week despite the Huang news and the biggest 2-year yield rise since 2022, with the S&P 500 about 2.5% below all-time highs.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Markets that rally through bad news signal a bottom and base-building; a tape-reading confirmation tool.
insights.quote: So if you can handle bad news, um that's a good sign

insights.claim: Visser says many investors who were forced to sell AI names the prior week for performance and risk-management reasons are now trapped by the sharp bounce and hoping for a chance to buy back.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Under-positioned managers chasing a rebound can fuel further upside in AI names.

insights.claim: Visser says Taiwan intervened in its market with a stabilization fund, and that Asian countries see an opportunity because they need higher stock markets to raise capital for AI.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Sovereign support in Asian equity markets is a tailwind for Asian AI supply-chain stocks.

themes.theme: Binance hack, AI-accelerated attacks and crypto resilience

insights.claim: According to CZ (relayed by Pompliano), Binance suffered roughly a $6 billion hack, and after frozen funds are returned it will be on the hook for about $3 billion.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: A ~$3B loss is a major hit to the largest exchange; monitor its balance sheet and user flows.

insights.claim: CZ told Pompliano that during the hack Binance froze withdrawals but not deposits, and users kept depositing to buy the dip after CZ said losses would be backstopped, which Pompliano calls one of the most bullish crypto data points he has heard.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Dip-buying deposits during an exchange hack signal deep retail conviction; Visser notes online sentiment instead blamed the hack for capitulation.
insights.quote: people were rushing to put assets on the platform to buy the dip

insights.claim: CZ said AI compressed the layered penetration of Binance's security, work that used to take months, into a matter of days; Visser says the only defense is AI agent swarms detecting and closing breaches, and notes the Binance hack involved human error in granting access.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: AI-on-AI cyber defense becomes mandatory spend for exchanges and financial firms; a tailwind for AI security vendors.
insights.quote: that's going to take AI fighting with AI. There's just no other way around it.

themes.theme: Convergence of AI, crypto and TradFi

insights.claim: Cantor Fitzgerald renamed its conference the Cantor Convergence conference, reflecting AI, crypto, energy infrastructure and quantum merging into one industry as banks, allocators and founders reach the same conclusion.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Institutional framing is shifting to a single convergence theme; expect more cross-sector capital.

insights.claim: Visser cites Marc Andreessen and Chris Dixon folding their crypto funds into broader frontier-style funds because there is no real difference between crypto and AI (e.g., Stripe spans both), which also drops the crypto label and broadens fundraising.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: VC rebranding of crypto into AI/frontier mandates signals capital flowing to crypto-AI crossover companies like payments.

insights.claim: Visser says the merger of AI, crypto and TradFi is happening and that tokenization and agentic commerce will grow daily, and once on-chain volumes become visible traditional investors will get excited.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Track on-chain tokenized-asset and agent-payment volumes as a leading indicator of institutional crypto inflows.
insights.quote: the merge of AI, the merge of crypto, and the merge of the TradFi world is happening
